ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a rectangular prism brick, with the areas of three adjacent faces labeled: the front face is labeled A, the top face is labeled B, and the right side face is labeled C. Let the three mutually perpendicular side lengths of the rectangular prism be x, y, z. The areas of the three adjacent faces are respectively the products of pairs of side lengths, so they can be recorded as A = xy, B = xz, C = yz (interchanging the specific side names does not affect the result). The volume of the rectangular prism is V = xyz. Multiply the three areas: ABC = (xy)(xz)(yz) = x^2y^2z^2 = (xyz)^2 = V^2. Because the volume is positive, V = sqrt(ABC).

raw_record.question_text: The faces of the brick have the areas A, B and C as shown. How big is the volume of the brick?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows a rectangular brick/cuboid with three mutually adjacent faces labeled A on the front face, B on the top face, and C on the right side face. Let the three edge lengths of the brick be x, y, and z. From the image, the three labeled face areas correspond to the pairwise products of these edge lengths, for example A = xy, B = xz, and C = yz up to naming of the edges. The volume is V = xyz. Multiply the three face-area equations: ABC = (xy)(xz)(yz) = x^2 y^2 z^2 = V^2. Since volume is positive, V = sqrt(ABC).
